html:
A magnitude 6.2 earthquake that struck Christchurch, the largest city of New Zealand's South Island, at lunchtime on 22 February 2011. It killed 185 people and destroyed much of the city centre.

It followed a larger quake in September 2010, the Canterbury earthquake, which had damaged buildings but killed no one. The February quake was smaller but centred much closer, only a few kilometres from downtown and very shallow, so the shaking was violent.

The worst single loss was the collapse of the CTV Building, where 115 people died, many of them foreign students at a language school. The spire of ChristChurch Cathedral, the city's symbol, fell. Across the eastern suburbs the ground turned to liquid and silt bubbled up through streets and homes.

The city centre was closed off for more than two years. Most of its tall buildings were pulled down, and whole suburbs along the river were abandoned as too risky to rebuild. The rebuilding cost tens of billions of dollars and is one of the largest in New Zealand history.
sum: A magnitude 6.2 earthquake that struck Christchurch, the largest city of New Zealand's South Island, at lunchtime on 22 February 2011. It killed 185 people and destroyed much of the city centre.
